memory_candidates.content: In-tree convention for keeping a restated enum in sync with a normative source (used when mechanical import into bash/markdown is impossible): restate the literals inline with a comment citing the normative file by path plus the exact phrase "keep this list and that table in sync rather than letting them drift independently" (established by scripts/command-gate-out.sh, reused by skill-orchestrate's Stage 5/MT-4 dispatch_status validation). Grep for this phrase to find all sync-comment sites drift-checking against a shared source.

Pseudo-instruction EXIT (partial)/EXIT (success)/EXIT (no-op) can appear inline inside an if/elif branch within a larger ```bash fenced block in SKILL.md files (see skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md's skeleton-exhaustion branch) -- it is documentation-level control flow for the agent reading the file, not literal bash, so bash -n checks on such blocks must be scoped to a sub-region (e.g. just the case block) that excludes it.

git-commit-scoped.sh's directory-glob positive pathspec (e.g. specs/{NNN}_{slug}/) combined with its auto-injected :(exclude) entries for ephemeral runtime files (.lock/, .orchestrator-loop-guard, etc.) can still trigger git's "paths ignored by .gitignore" hard error on `git add`, aborting the whole scoped commit (exit 2) even though the excludes are textually correct. Workaround: stage the specific non-ignored files individually (git add <file1> <file2> ...) instead of the directory glob when this happens, rather than reaching for `git add -f` (which would force-add the ignored ephemeral files into history).
